citation: Stokes, L., Hudson-Sharp, N., Dorsett, R., Rolfe, H., Anders, J., George, A., Buzzeo, J., & Munro-Lott, N. (2018). Mathematical Reasoning: Evaluation report and executive summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation.
report_number: EEF project: Mathematical Reasoning (effectiveness trial), December 2018
design: Cluster (school-level) RCT. 169 schools randomised at the school level (84 intervention / 85 control; 7,419 pupils); 160 schools (80/80) took the post-test; analysis sample 6,353 pupils (3,238 intervention / 3,115 control). Subject = mathematics; pupils in Year 2 (England), i.e. grade band K-2. Single intervention arm vs business-as-usual control (wait-list, received programme the following year). Intervention = Mathematical Reasoning programme (Nunes & Bryant, University of Oxford), 10 units taught by class teachers over 12-15 weeks within normal maths lessons.
problems: Subject is mathematics (STEM), NOT Reading -- the only local row carrying a 'Reading' subject for this study, data/extracted/effect_sizes_FIXTURE.csv (es_id F0286), is explicitly a SYNTHETIC FIXTURE (random outcome_subject, random n's) and was NOT used. The Visscher et al. (2025) supplement (S3.1/S3.2 = registry row 116) codes only School/RCT/Unpublished/K-2/Average-High SES/All; (P)CK/Short/External/coaching=1 -- it gives no subject and no citation. Identification rests on a tight match of every available moderator (see notes below), with Stokes as first author. The g standardises an ANCOVA (school-level KS1 prior-attainment-adjusted) treatment coefficient by the pooled UNADJUSTED outcome SD, per the EEF Hedges-g formula; SE/variance are back-computed from the reported 95% CI (the report gives no SE directly). Cluster-robust SEs (Stata cluster on school) were used, so the estimate is cluster-adjusted; ICC not reported in the report (left null -- not guessed).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Mathematical Reasoning vs business-as-usual control (single arm)
effect_sizes.test_name: Progress Test in Maths (PTM, GL Assessment) - standard age score
effect_sizes.g_method: EEF Hedges' g: adjusted treatment-group difference (beta = 1.181, ANCOVA adjusting for school-level KS1 prior attainment) standardised by the pooled UNADJUSTED outcome SD (pooled variance 242.80 -> SD 15.58); 1.181/15.58 = 0.076 ~ 0.08 reported (Hedges J ~= 1.000 for this df, negligible). g_se and g_var back-computed from the reported 95% CI (-0.03, 0.18): SE = (0.18-(-0.03))/(2*1.96) = 0.0536, var = 0.00287. sd_t/sd_c derived as sqrt(group outcome variances 238.97 and 246.77 from Table 7.
effect_sizes.notes: Headline confirmatory outcome. p=0.156, n.s. (below the 0.14 MDES). Cluster-robust SEs (Stata cluster option on school); analysis on complete cases. This is the EFFECTIVENESS trial (train-the-trainers via Maths Hubs / NCETM, reduced developer involvement), distinct from the earlier developer-led EFFICACY trial ('Improving Numeracy and Literacy in Key Stage 1', Worth et al.) which reported a larger ES (~0.2).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Mathematical Reasoning vs control -- FSM-eligible subgroup
effect_sizes.test_name: Progress Test in Maths (PTM, GL Assessment) - standard age score
effect_sizes.g_method: EEF Hedges' g: adjusted difference 1.31 standardised by pooled unadjusted SD (pooled variance 217.53 -> SD 14.75); g=0.09 reported. g_se/g_var back-computed from reported 95% CI (-0.07, 0.25): SE = (0.25-(-0.07))/(2*1.96) = 0.0816, var = 0.006664. sd_t/sd_c from group variances 221.29 and 213.91 (Table 9).
effect_sizes.notes: Pre-specified FSM-eligible subgroup (non-randomised subset). p=0.288, n.s. Not the full-sample contrast; provided for completeness and excluded by is_full_sample=false.
